name: ACTIVATED PARTIAL THROMBOPLASTIN TIME
description: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) measures intrinsic coagulation pathway and evaluates heparin therapy, factor deficiencies, and lupus anticoagulant. This test assesses contact activation factors and common pathway.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Beckman Coulter, Roche Cobas, Abbott Architect

literatureReview: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) measures the intrinsic coagulation pathway, assessing factors VIII, IX, XI, XII, and common pathway factors. Normal range 20-40 seconds. Prolonged APTT indicates heparin therapy, factor deficiencies (hemophilia), von Willebrand disease, or lupus anticoagulant. Clot-based assay using phospholipid and activator. Critical for monitoring unfractionated heparin (target 1.5-2.5 × normal). Used in screening for bleeding disorders and evaluation of prolonged PT/APTT. APTT is more sensitive to intrinsic pathway abnormalities than PT. Mixing studies help distinguish factor deficiencies from inhibitors. Essential test in coagulation workup and anticoagulation monitoring.
